chunks: What Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from some of our companions, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, who said:
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام led us in prayer, and in the first rakʿah he recited وَالضُّحَى, and in the second, أَلَمْ نَشْرَحْ.

So this narration, even though it indicates that he recited them in the two rakʿahs, does not state that he recited them in an obligatory prayer or a supererogatory prayer. It is possible that he recited them in two rakʿahs of supererogatory prayers, and that is permissible, as we have explained.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, the one described as leading the prayer
key_terms.الثَّانِيَةِ: the second rakʿah of the prayer
key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ: the two units of prayer in which the recitation occurred
key_terms.النَّوَافِلِ: optional prayers beyond the obligatory ones
key_terms.الْأُولَى: the first rakʿah of the prayer

ai.seo_question: Does this narration prove that combining or pairing these surahs is allowed in the obligatory prayer?
ai.summary: This report states that Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام recited Sūrat al-Ḍuḥā in the first rakʿah and Sūrat Alam Nashraḥ in the second. The accompanying legal clarification argues that the report does not prove this occurred in an obligatory prayer, and it may have been in a supererogatory prayer where such recitation is permissible.
